headline: High-risk shared-file and server-side execution paths make Langflow→pdf.js interactions vulnerable to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write/read filesystem and chain tools in flows, so attacker-controlled content can reach downstream steps. pdf.js reads PDF files and runs in browser-based tests, making PDF content a plausible injection carrier if its output is fed into Langflow. The shared-file pathway is documented, but not a direct parser bridge, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF a PDF uploaded to pdf.js is later ingested by a Langflow flow without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Langflow nodes treat file text as instructions, attacker-controlled PDF content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add a sanitization step before Langflow ingests any PDF-derived text.
Use a strict allowlist for flow nodes that consume document text.
Separate upload folders for pdf.js and Langflow.
Disable automatic execution of document-derived instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from pdf.js into Langflow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored secrets on the server filesystem; pdf.js processes PDF documents locally with file access. If both share a workspace, sensitive PDF contents can be copied into Langflow outputs or logs. pdf.js has no network egress, which limits exfiltration, but the shared-file path still creates a medium leakage risk.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory, PDF contents may be exposed to Langflow.
IF Langflow stores flow outputs containing document text, sensitive data can persist beyond pdf.js processing.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Restrict Langflow logs to redact document text.
Store PDFs in a read-only input directory.
Delete intermediate exports after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has server-side write access and can execute shell/subprocesses; pdf.js reads PDFs and runs browser-based tests. They do not both advertise unrestricted write to the same mutable resource, but Langflow’s shared server-side state plus concurrent instances creates a plausible conflict if both touch the same workspace or flow artifacts. Uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Langflow flows mutate shared artifacts while pdf.js tests read them, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run pdf.js in read-only mode.
Serialize access to shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent writes from Langflow flows.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream steps. pdf.js processes PDFs and can supply extracted text or rendered content into Langflow flows. Because the pair can form an A→B pipeline without a built-in verification step, cascading errors are plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF Langflow consumes pdf.js output without validation, extraction errors can propagate.
IF downstream flow nodes act on document text as facts, incorrect PDF parsing can trigger wrong actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action-taking nodes.
Compare extracted text against the source PDF for spot checks.
Mark pdf.js output as untrusted in the flow.
Limit downstream actions to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add verification nodes between pdf.js and Langflow actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not specify conflicting residency, certification, or retention regimes. Langflow stores flow inputs and secrets server-side, while pdf.js handles PDF files locally, but no explicit compliance mismatch is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise policy mismatch, though no breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF a deployment routes regulated PDFs into Langflow storage with stricter retention rules than pdf.js, policy mismatch may arise.
IF an operator requires residency guarantees not stated in either profile, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Document retention rules for both tools.
Keep regulated PDFs out of Langflow storage.
Review deployment residency settings.
Delete temporary PDF artifacts promptly.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated document classes.
